epochNote: year 0 = first sunrise (F.A. 1); Y.T. at 1 V.Y.=9.582 sun-years [I-H] — the Annals of Aman figure, which its own source gives as a revision of an earlier exactly-10 (NoME, on the c.1951 revisions to the Annals of Aman); the corpus holds three schemes (10, 9.582, 144) and arda_reckoning.json displays all three without resolving them. A numeric axis needs one constant; the choice is the archive's [conflict]; S.A.=+590; T.A.=+4031; F.o.A.=+7052

eras.label: Valian Years before the Trees
eras.note: THE ANNALS OF AMAN COUNT TWICE. Valian Years run 1 to 3500 BEFORE the Trees, then the count RESTARTS at Y.T. 1. Two clocks, not one long one, so they carry distinct era ids and a sort can never mix them -- his ruling C846. The span is 33,550 axis units = 3,501 Valian Years at the 9.582 sun-year constant this file's own epochNote declares, marks [I-H], and already uses for every published Y.T. event. Extending an axis the archive chose is not choosing a scheme: the corpus holds three (10, 9.582, 144) and arda_reckoning.json still displays all three unresolved.

events.label: Melkor claims the kingship of Arda and mars all that the other Valar make
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Valar descend into Arda and begin the shaping of its lands and waters
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Arda is ordered and made ready, and the Valar dwell upon the Isle of Almaren
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Aulë makes the two lamps, Illuin and Ormal, and Varda fills them with hallowed fire
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Manwë ordains a great feast upon Almaren and summons all the Valar
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melkor gathers perverted spirits, and Sauron of Aulë's household is his chief spy
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Tulkas comes to Arda; Melkor flees before him, and there is a long peace
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: At the feast of the Spring of Arda, Tulkas espouses Nessa
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melkor delves Utumno, and the Spring of Arda is marred
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Then Tulkas slept, being weary and content, and Melkor deemed that his hour had come. And he passed, therefore, over the Walls of the Night19 with his host, and he came to Middle-earth in the North; and the Valar were not aware of him.
events.cite: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melkor casts down the pillars of Illuin and Ormal, and Arda is marred
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melkor escapes to Utumno, and the Valar cannot at that time overcome him
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Middle-earth lies in twilight beneath the stars, and the Valar come seldom thither
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Spring of Arda ends; the Valar remove to Aman and raise the Pelóri
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Days of the Bliss of Valinor begin, and with them the count of Time
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Two Trees awake: Telperion the elder and Laurelin the younger
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Valar build Valmar the Blessed, and a green mound stands before its gate
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Varda hoards the light of the Trees in mighty vats nigh the Green Mound
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Yavanna sings upon the Green Mound, and two saplings spring from it
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Music of the Ainur; the Valar enter Eä (both before the count of years) — the Lamps are LATER and dated: AAm §14 sets them up in V.Y. 1900, 'Illuin and Ormal they were named. 1900 And they were set upon mighty pillars'; how long they stood is unstated
events.cite: Ainulindalë; Silm 1; AAm §14 (HoME X) for the Lamps

events.label: For a thousand years of the Trees the Valar dwell in bliss in Valinor
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melkor breeds the Balrogs in Utumno.
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Oromë rides often to Middle-earth to hunt under the stars
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Two Trees first bloom
events.cite: Silm 7; HoME X AAm

events.label: But Mandos spoke and said that though the Coming was prepared it should not yet be for many Years; and the Elder Children should come in the darkness and look first upon the Stars. For so it was ordained.
events.cite: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Valar hold council, and Yavanna beseeches Manwë to give light to Middle-earth
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Varda begins the great labour of the stars
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Varda makes new stars and sets the signs of heaven, greatest Menelmakar
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Awakening of the Elves at Cuiviénen
events.cite: HoME X AAm ('450 such Years before' F.A.)

events.label: At this time also, it is said, Melian, fairest of the Maiar, desiring to look upon the stars, went up upon Taniquetil; and suddenly she desired to see Middle-earth, and she left Valinor and walked in the twilight.
events.cite: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Hither, it is said, at this time came Melian the Maia from Valinor, when Varda made the great stars. In this same time the Quendi awoke by Kuiviénen, as is told in the Chronicle of Aman.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Last of all Varda made the sign of bright stars that is called the Valakirka, the Sickle of the Gods, and this she hung about the North as a threat unto Utumno and a token of the doom of Melkor.
events.cite: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Quendi make speech, and name themselves those that speak with voices
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: About this time the spies of Melkor discovered the Quendi and afflicted them.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: In this year Oromë found the Quendi, and befriended them.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Melkor's shadows waylay the straying Quendi, and they fear the Rider
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Oromë finds the Quendi and names them Eldar, the people of the stars
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Oromë, hunting under the Orokarni, hears the Quendi singing
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Some Quendi hide or flee at Oromë's coming; those who stay are unafraid
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Quendi taken into Utumno are corrupted and enslaved: thus Melkor breeds the Orkor
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Oromë brings tidings to Valinor; the Valar debate the guarding of the Quendi
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Manwë resolves on war; the Valar assail Melkor for the Elves' sake and defeat him
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melkor driven back to Utumno; a guard set over Kuiviénen; after two years the siege begins
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Valar come from Aman to assault Melkor, and the War of the Powers breaks the shape of the land.
The long siege of Utumno; Middle-earth shaken and the far North made desolate
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Utumno's gates broken; the Balrogs destroyed; Tulkas binds Melkor with Angainor
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melkor brought bound to the Ring of Doom; his plea denied, he is shut in Mandos
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melkor doomed to three ages in Mandos; the Noontide of the Blessed Realm begins
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Valar summon the Quendi to Aman; Oromë bears the message to Kuiviénen
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Ingwë, Finwë, and Elwë were brought to Valinor by Oromë as ambassadors of the Quendi and they looked upon the Light of the Trees and yearned for it. Returning they counselled the Eldar to go to the Land of Aman, at the summons of the Valar.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: The Quendi are dismayed; Oromë chooses Ingwë, Finwë and Elwë as ambassadors
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The three Elf-lords were brought, therefore, to Valmar, and there spoke with Manwë and the Valar; and they were filled with awe, but the beauty and splendour of the land of Valinor overcame their fear, and they desired the Light of the Trees.
events.cite: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: And after they had dwelt in Valinor a while, Oromë brought them back to Kuiviénen, and they spoke before their people and counselled them to heed the summons of the Valar and remove into the West.
events.cite: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Great March (Anduin reached 1115)
events.cite: HoME X AAm; NoME

events.label: The first sundering: Eldar and Avari, the Unwilling, part at Kuiviénen
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: After ten Years the Eldar come to a great river with mountains beyond
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Nano, called Dân, forsakes the March and leads his folk south: the Nandor
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Oromë brings the Vanyar and Noldor to the shores of Beleriand, and they draw back in fear of the Sea.
The March goes slow; the Eldar halt whenever Oromë leaves them
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Vanyar and Noldor cross Anduin to the Hithaeglir; the Teleri linger on the east bank
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Vanyar and Noldor cross into Beleriand and reach the Great Sea
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Teleri come over Eryd Luin into northern Beleriand.
The Teleri come to Beleriand and dwell beyond Gelion
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Elwë Singollo is lost in Nan Elmoth, where he finds Melian; thus began their love.
Elwë strays into Nan Elmoth and finds Melian; his people seek him in vain
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Teleri remain behind and take Olwë for their lord; Ossë and Uinen teach them sea-lore.
The Teleri stay behind, take Olwë for king, and learn sea-lore of Ossë and Uinen.
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Ulmo bears the Vanyar and Noldor over Sea upon an island; the Isle of Balar is broken from it.
Ulmo draws the isle of Eressëa to Aman, bearing the Vanyar and the Noldor
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Kalakiryan cleft; Túna raised, and Tirion the Hallowed built upon it
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Tirion full-wrought and the Mindon Eldaliéva raised; Ingwë departs to Valinor
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Eldar come to Aman; Tirion and Alqualondë built
events.cite: Silm 5; AAm

events.label: In this year Yavanna gave to the Noldor the White Tree, Galathilion, image of the Tree Telperion, and it was planted beneath the Mindon and grew and flourished.
events.cite: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Ossë persuades many Teleri to remain; they become the mariners of the Falas under Círdan.
Ulmo returns for the Teleri; Ossë keeps some on the coasts of Beleriand, Círdan their lord
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Ulmo returns to Beleriand to bear the Teleri to Aman, but Ossë is ill-pleased.
Olwë's folk borne away upon Eressëa; those left behind become the Eglath, the Forsaken
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The friends of Elwë are left behind, and call themselves the Eglath, the Forsaken People.
At Ossë's call Ulmo roots Eressëa in the Sea, within sight of Aman
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Valar ill-pleased at Ulmo's deed; Finwë grieves for Elwë forsaken
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Elwë awakes and comes forth from Nan Elmoth with Melian, and is made King of the Eglath.
Elwë wakes from his trance: Elu Thingol, King of the Sindar, with Melian his Queen
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Ossë teaches the Teleri shipbuilding; drawn by swans they come to Eldamar
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: In this year Olwë lord of the Teleri, with the aid of Finwë and the Noldor, began the building of Alqualondë, the Swanhaven, upon the coast of Eldamar, north of the Kalakiryan.
events.cite: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: In this year the last of the Vanyar departed from Tirion, and the Noldor dwelt there alone, and their converse and friendship thereafter was rather with the Teleri.
events.cite: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Birth of Fëanor, eldest son of Finwë, in Tirion; his mother Byrde Míriel
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Rúmil devises letters, and first writes the tongues of the Eldar
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Noldor surpass their teachers; the masons of Finwë's house find the earth-gems
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: In this year was born Fingolfin son of Finwë, who after was King of the Exiles.
events.cite: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: It is held that Lúthien, only child of Elwë and Melian, was born in Neldoreth.
The power of Elwë and Melian reaches over all Beleriand; his people are named the Sindar.
Finrod Finwë’s son was born.
events.cite: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Fëanor devises the Tengwar
events.cite: App E; Silm 6; NoME; AAm 1250 §83 (HoME X) — 'In this time began the flowering of the skill of Fëanor son of Finwë, who was of all the Noldor the greatest maker and craftsman. And he took thought and devised new letters'

events.label: Elves and Dwarves learn each other's speech, and Thingol welcomes them.
Fëanor betters the letters of Rúmil, and studies the making of gems
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Dwarves come first over the mountains into Beleriand, out of Belegost and Nogrod.
The Naugrim come into Beleriand; Belegost helps Thingol delve Menegroth
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: In this year Finrod Finwë’s son wedded Ëarwen King Olwë’s daughter of Alqualondë, and there was a great feast in the land of the Teleri. Thus the children of Finrod, Inglor and Galadriel, were the kin of King Thingol Greymantle in Beleriand.
events.cite: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: At Melian's counsel Thingol calls on the Dwarves of Belegost to build him a kingly dwelling.
Elves and Dwarves adorn Menegroth with the visions of Melian.
Peace in Thingol's realm; but the Dwarves bring word of fell beasts abroad east of the mountains.
The Naugrim delve Menegroth, the Thousand Caves, for Thingol above the Esgalduin.
Evil creatures come into Beleriand over the passes: wolves, and other fell beings of shadow.
Orcs first come into Beleriand, few and wary, awaiting the return of their Lord.
The Sindar, now well armed, drive off the creatures of evil and have peace again.
Thingol takes thought for arms, and the Naugrim first smithy weapons for him.
Dairon the minstrel, chief loremaster of Thingol, devises his Runes.
Denethor leads the Nandor into Beleriand; they dwell in Ossiriand and are called the Green-elves.
The Green-elves come to Ossiriand under Denethor son of Dân
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melkor unchained
events.cite: Silm 6; AAm

events.label: And Niënna aided his prayer (because of her kinship), and Manwë granted it, for being himself free of all evil he saw not the depths of the heart of Melkor, and believed in his oaths. But Mandos was silent, and Ulmo’s heart misgave him.
events.cite: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melkor, his three ages served, comes before the Valar and sues for pardon
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melkor betrays the clemency of Manwë; a shadow falls and the golden Noon passes
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melkor dwells under vigilance in Valmar; Manwë grants him freedom in Valinor
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melkor feigns friendship and teaches the Noldor; the Vanyar refuse him
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Fëanor conceives the Silmarils and begins the work
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Silmarils wrought
events.cite: Silm 7; AAm

events.label: Melkor seeks to destroy Fëanor and unmake the friendship of Valar and Eldar
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melkor's lie of Fingolfin breeds quarrel; swords are drawn in Eldamar
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melkor's lies run in Eldamar; he foretells the coming of Men
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Noldor murmur against the Valar, and first smithy swords, axes and shields
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Varda hallows the Silmarils; Melkor lusts after them
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Fëanor banished from Tirion; he builds Formenos, and Finwë goes with him
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Tulkas seeks Melkor, but he has hidden himself; the Light of the Trees dims
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: And at that time, being himself in peril, Melkor departed, consumed with wrath, and bitter vengeance he plotted for his shame. But Finwë was filled with great fear, and in haste he sent messengers to Manwë in Valmar.
events.cite: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Fëanor perceives Melkor's lust for the Silmarils, curses him and shuts his doors
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melkor comes to Arvalin, where Ungoliantë dwells in a cleft of the mountains
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melkor comes to Formenos and tempts Finwë and Fëanor
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melkor demands Ungoliantë's aid, and vows her a reward
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melkor flees through the Kalakiryan; the pursuit fails and the shadow lifts
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Darkening of Valinor; Kinslaying at Alqualondë; the Flight
events.cite: Silm 8–9; AAm 1495 §107 (HoME X) [C]

events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Fëanor comes to Alqualondë to win the Teleri and their ships

events.label: The herald departs and the Noldor march on, the House of Fëanor in the van
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The hour of a high feast in Valinor, as Melkor well knew
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The lights named: Isil and Anar by the Vanyar, Rána and Vása by the Noldor
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The pursuit of Melkor fails: the riders are blinded in Ungoliantë's Cloud
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Ungoliantë comes into Thingol's realm and is stayed by Melian; she abides under Eryd Orgoroth.
Valmar founders in night; all song ceases save the wailing of the Teleri
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Vanyar, Noldor, Maiar and Valar keep the feast on Taniquetil; Valmar stands empty
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Word from Formenos: Melkor has slain Finwë and taken the Silmarils
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Yavanna asks Fëanor for the Silmarils, that she may recall the Trees to life
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Yavanna fears the Great Darkness; the doom of the Noldor draws nigh
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: At the borders of Araman a dark figure bids the Noldor stand and give ear
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Finrod turns back, is pardoned, and rules the remnant of the Noldor in Aman
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Fëanor keeps the Oath, and dooms the Noldor's deeds to be matter of song
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Doom on the House of Fëanor: their Oath shall betray them; the Dispossessed
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Doom: for blood spilled ye shall render blood, and dwell in Death's shadow
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Prophecy of the North: turn back, or Valinor shall be fenced against you
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: First Battle of Beleriand: Denethor falls; the Girdle of Melian raised
events.cite: Silm 10; GA 1497 §36 (HoME XI) — 'In this year Morgoth made his first assault upon Beleriand, which lay south of Angband'

events.label: 'None and none!' -- Fëanor bids the ships be burned
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: A coolness stands from the first between Thingol and the sons of Fëanor.
Dagor-nuin-Giliath, the Battle under the Stars: Morgoth's host is destroyed in ten days' fighting.
Denethor falls upon Amon Ereb, and the Green-elves take no king again.
Fingolfin, betrayed, leads his host over the Helkaraxë into Endar
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Fëanor dies upon the slopes of Eryd-wethrin, laying his oath upon his sons.
Fëanor halts; the host murmurs, and two ways only are seen -- the ice or the ships
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Fëanor lands in the Firth of Drengist and burns the ships at Losgar.
Fëanor seizes the ships and sails, leaving Fingolfin; he lands at Drengist
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Fëanor, far ahead of his host, is surrounded by Balrogs and smitten down by Gothmog.

In this year Morgoth made his first assault upon Beleriand, which lay south of Angband. Indeed it is said that the gates of Morgoth were but one hundred and fifty leagues distant from the bridge of Menegroth; far and yet all too near.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Maidros asks what ships shall return, and whom they shall bear over first
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Melian sets her Girdle about the realm, and Eglador is thereafter called Doriath.
Morgoth and Maidros come to a feigned parley, and Maidros is taken captive.
Morgoth holds Maidros hostage against the departure of the Noldor.
The Noldor come to the Helkaraxë, the grinding strait
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Orcs assail Thingol's realm and cut him off from Círdan at Eglarest.
The burning at Losgar is seen by Fingolfin and by the watchers of Morgoth.
The burning of the ships at Losgar; Fingolfin's people see the light afar
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The first battle of the Wars of Beleriand: the eastern Orc-host is destroyed between Aros and Gelion.
The host of Fëanor passes into Hithlum and encamps about Lake Mithrim.
Tidings of the Noldor come to Menegroth, but Thingol welcomes them not with full heart.
Morgoth hangs Maidros from the west-tower of Thangorodrim; his brethren fortify a camp in Hithlum.
Helcaraxë crossing; first Moonrise
events.cite: Silm 9/11; AAm

events.label: The Sun first rises, and the First Age is reckoned from it (Dagor-nuin-Giliath and the death of Fëanor fall BEFORE it, under Y.T. 1497 — GA §36–44: 'the Battle under the Stars, for the Moon had not yet risen')
events.cite: Silm 11/13; GA 1497 §36–44 (HoME XI) — the battle and Fëanor's death fall under Y.T. 1497, 'the Battle under the Stars, for the Moon had not yet risen'; only the sunrise is F.A. 1

events.label: Fingolfin's host crosses the grinding ice of Helkaraxë; the ages of the Stars end.
Isil rises first; Fingolfin enters the Northern Lands at the first moonrise, and Anar arises
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Morgoth assails Tilion and is worsted; he fears Arien, and hides in cloud
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Hiding of Valinor: the Enchanted Isles set, and the Realm shut against the Noldor
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Moon is bidden rise after the Sun descends; Tilion is drawn ever to Arien
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The Pelóri raised sheer and a sleepless watch set; only the Kalakiryan is left open
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: The light of the Trees lives now in the Silmarils alone, and they are lost
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Thereafter the Valar reckon the days by the coming and going of Anar
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Varda allows a time of shadow: Anar rests a while in Valinor
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: Varda sets the courses of Sun and Moon; but Tilion is wayward
events.src: HoMe X, The Annals of Aman

events.label: At the first Sunrise Men awake in Hildorien, and are named the Atani.
From this time are reckoned the Years of the Sun, and all things grow in the Second Spring of Arda.
Morgoth assails Tilion; then comes the first Dawn of the Sun, and Fingolfin unfurls his banners.
Morgoth withdraws into the depths of Angband, and Fingolfin smites upon its gates unopposed.
The Moon rises new, and Fingolfin begins his march into Middle-earth.
Fingolfin comes to Hithlum and camps by the north shore of Lake Mithrim.
Morgoth's smokes darken the new Sun over Hithlum and lie poisonous upon Mithrim.
The people of Fëanor withdraw to the south shore, and the Lake lies between the hosts.
Fingon rescues Maidros from Thangorodrim by the aid of Thorondor, severing his hand.
Maedhros rescued from Thangorodrim
events.cite: Silm 13; GA 1498 §51 (HoME XI) [I-M] — the archive's own year for the RESCUE. The annal dates the HANGING, in the Years of the Trees: 'Therefore Morgoth took Maidros, and setting a band of hellwrought steel about his right wrist hung him thereby above a precipice upon the west-tower of Thangorodrim'. No annal I have found dates Fingon's rescue

events.label: Angrod is the first of the Exiles to come to Menegroth, and tells Thingol of the Noldor.
The Noldor, again united, watch the borders of Dor-Daedeloth and send messengers through Beleriand.
Thingol grants the Noldor Hithlum, Dorthonion and the lands east of Doriath, and claims Beleriand.
Angrod goes wroth from the council, and the Noldor are troubled at the sons of Fëanor.
Cranthir cries out against the sons of Finrod for bearing tales to the Dark-elf in his caves.
Fingolfin is chosen overlord of the Exiles; Maidros alone of Fëanor's sons takes it well.
Maidros answers Thingol's words, saying he grants only lands where his power does not run.
The Noldor hold council in Mithrim on the Grey-elves and the war upon Morgoth.
The sons of Fëanor leave Mithrim for the lands thereafter called the March of Maidros.

(At this feast it is recorded that the tongue of the Grey-elves was most spoken even by the Noldor, for whereas the Noldor readily learned the speech of the land, the Sindar were slow to master the tongue of Aman.)
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Fingolfin holds the feast Mereth Aderthad by the pools of Ivrin; Thingol sends but two messengers.
Mereth Aderthad, the Feast of Reuniting
events.cite: Silm 13; GA 20 §72 (HoME XI) — 'In this year Fingolfin, King of the Noldor, called a great council and made a high feast, that was long after remembered'

events.label: Ulmo troubles Inglor and Turgon in dreams, and each seeks a place of refuge.
Inglor, guest of Thingol, is shown the caves of Narog and begins Nargothrond; he is named Felagund.
Nargothrond founded by Finrod
events.cite: Silm 13; GA 52 §75 (HoME XI) [C] — 'that stronghold was called Nargothrond. Wherefore the Noldor named him Felagund, Lord of Caves'. The annal names him INGLOR; in the Grey Annals 'Finrod' means Finarfin, the father.

events.label: Ulmo appears to Turgon at Nivrost, and he discovers the hidden vale of Gondolin.
Dagor Aglareb: the Orc-host is driven onto Ardgalen and destroyed within sight of Angband.
Dagor Aglareb; the Siege of Angband begins
events.cite: Silm 13; GA 60, The Third Battle §77 (HoME XI) — 'Here Morgoth... made trial of the strength and watchfulness of his enemies'

events.label: Fingolfin and Fingon hold Hithlum from Eithel Sirion, with horsemen upon Ardgalen.
Fingolfin boasts that save by treason Morgoth can never again burst from the leaguer of the Eldar.
In the peace of the Siege Men wax and multiply, and the Atanatári move ever westward.
Inglor builds the watchtower Minnas-tirith in the pass of Sirion, and sets Orodreth as warden.
Morgoth bids the Orcs take the Eldar alive and bring them bound to Angband.
Morgoth, afraid of the growing union of the Eldar, comes back to Angband.
The Eldar learn from captives that the Silmarils are set in Morgoth's Iron Crown.
The lands south of the March of Maidros are held the domain of the sons of Fëanor.

The sons of Finrod held the land from Hithlum unto the eastern end of Dorthonion. Inglor and Orodreth held the pass of Sirion, but Angrod and Egnor held the north slopes of Dorthonion as far as Aglon where began the March of Maidros aforesaid.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Turgon leads his most skilled folk secretly to Gondolin, and they begin the building of the city.
Brithombar and Eglarest are walled about, and the Tower of Ingildon is set up to watch the Sea.
Galadriel dwells with Melian, but will not speak of the death of the Trees.
Galadriel tells Melian of the Silmarils and the slaying of Finwë, but not of the Oath.
Melian asks Galadriel what woe lies upon her kin, and is not answered.
Melian bids Thingol beware the sons of Fëanor, on whom the wrath of the Gods lies.
Melian says she sees evil on the road from Tirion, which Thingol should learn.
Melian says the Noldor came not as messengers of the Valar, and asks why they were exiled.
Melian tells Thingol of the Silmarils, and that Morgoth slew Finwë ere he fled from Aman.
Thingol answers that the Noldor came for vengeance, yet will be the surer allies.
Thingol calls Fëanor's sons the deadliest foes of his foe; Melian says their counsels have two edges.
Angrod speaks out against the sons of Fëanor, telling of the blood at Alqualondë and the burning of the ships.

But Inglor answered: ‘What ill have I done thee, lord? Or what evil deed have the Noldor done in all thy realm to grieve thee? Neither against thy kingship nor against any of thy folk have they thought evil or done evil.’
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Dark tales of the Noldor pass among the Sindar, and Círdan sends word of them to Thingol.
The Sindar refuse the tongue of the Noldor, and the Exiles take Sindarin for daily use.
Thingol bids the sons of Finrod go, but will not shut his doors against them for ever.
Thingol forbids the tongue of the Noldor to be spoken openly in all his realm.
Thingol speaks in ire to Inglor, saying he has learned of all the evil deeds of the Noldor.

‘I marvel at thee, son of Eärwen,’ said Thingol, ‘that thou wouldst come to the board of thy kinsman thus red-handed from the slaying of thy mother’s kin, and yet say nought in defence, nor yet seek any pardon!’
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: But it is said that not until that hour had such cold thoughts ruled him; for indeed she whom he had loved was Amárië of the Vanyar, and she was not permitted to go with him into exile.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Nargothrond is full-wrought; Felagund foretells that he shall swear an oath and leave no heir.
Gondolin full-wrought (52 years of toil)
events.cite: Silm 15; GA 116 §110 (HoME XI) [C] — 'Gondolin was full-wrought, in fifty years after the coming of Turgon from Nivrost'.

events.label: Turgon leads his folk secretly to Gondolin and the gates are shut; Nivrost is left empty.
Ulmo bids Turgon leave arms in Vinyamar, by which he shall know the messenger to come.
Ulmo comes a second time to Turgon at Vinyamar and bids him go at last to Gondolin.
Cranthir's folk first come upon the Naugrim, and the two peoples make alliance.
An army sent by the white north to Drengist is trapped, and the Orcs driven into the sea.
Glaurung first issues from Angband — driven back by Fingon
events.cite: Silm 13; GA 260 §116 (HoME XI) — 'Here Glaurung, the first of the Urulóki, the fire-drakes of the North, came forth from Angband's gate by night'

events.label: Glaurung, yet half-grown, defiles Ardgalen and is driven back by Fingon's horsed archers.
Finrod finds the Edain in Ossiriand
events.cite: Silm 17 [I-M] on the year — THE RECENSIONS DISAGREE. The Grey Annals date the meeting to 400, 'came upon Bëor' (header verified), on a chronology where Bëor is born 370; the Later Quenta gives Bëor 262–355, and c.310 belongs to that later history. The archive follows the Later Quenta and the annal is the other tradition.

events.label: Isfin goes from Gondolin and comes to Nan Elmoth, where Ëol takes her to wife.
Isfin bears a son to Ëol in Nan Elmoth, whom his father names Glindûr (later Maeglin).
Here Bëor, eldest of the Fathers of Men of the West, was born east of the mountains.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Here Haleth the Hunter was born in Eriador.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Here also in Eriador was born Hador the Golden-haired, whose house was after the most renowned of all the kindreds of the Elf-friends.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Felagund comes upon Bëor and his men in Ossiriand, and Bëor becomes his vassal.
Isfin and her son flee to Gondolin; Ëol slays her with a poisoned dart and is cast from the walls.
Bëor is the first of Men to draw sword for the Eldar, at the pass of Aglon.
Hundor son of Haleth was born.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Galion the Tall, son of Hador, was born in Eriador.
Gundor son of Hador was born beneath the shadows of Eryd Lindon.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Haleth and Hador come into Beleriand; Haleth dwells in Brethil, and Hador in Dor-lómin.
Melian foretells that a man of Bëor's house shall pass the Girdle of Melian.
Thingol confines Men to Hithlum and Dorthonion, and forbids any Man to enter Doriath.
Fingolfin ponders an assault upon Angband, but his designs are delayed and come to naught.
Here at the prayer of Inglor Thingol granted to Haleth’s people to live in Brethil; for they were in good friendship with the woodland Elves.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: The Men of the Three Houses grow and multiply, learning wisdom and craft of the Eldar.
Baragund son of Bregolas son of Bëor was born in Dorthonion.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Hador's folk entered Dor-lómin.
Belegund his brother was born.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Beren son of Barahir son of Bëor was born in Dorthonion, who was after named Erchamion the One-handed and Camlost the Emptyhanded. His mother was Emeldir the Manhearted.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Hundor son of Haleth wedded Glorwendil daughter of Hador.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Húrin the Steadfast son of Galion son of Hador was born in Hithlum. In the same year was born Handir son of Hundor.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Morwen Eleðwen, the Elf-sheen, was born, daughter of Baragund. She was the fairest of all mortal maidens of the Elder Days.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Huor brother of Húrin was born.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Bëor the Old dies of age, the first waning of the life of Men the Eldar had seen; Bregolas rules after him.
Rían daughter of Belegund is born.
Angrod and Egnor fall on Dorthonion; Barahir saves Felagund in the Fen of Serech and is given his ring.
Dagor Bragollach; Fingolfin falls before Angband
events.cite: Silm 18; GA 455 §145 (HoME XI) [C]

events.label: Hador falls at Eithel Sirion with Gundor his son, and Galion takes the lordship of his House.
Sauron takes Minnas-tirith upon Tol Sirion, and Orodreth is driven out to Nargothrond.
The Fell Year: the Dagor Bragollach begins at mid-winter, and Ardgalen is burned into the Anfauglith.
The March of Maidros is overwhelmed; Himring holds, but the Orcs ravage East Beleriand.
Tol Sirion becomes accursed and is called Tol-in-Gaurhoth, the Isle of Werewolves.
Turgon was not in that battle, nor Haleth, nor any but few of Haleth's men.
Turgon's messengers essay to build ships to seek Valinor, but all founder or are driven back.
Emeldir leads the women and children of Dorthonion to Brethil; Barahir and twelve are left outlawed.
Fingolfin pins Morgoth's foot with Ringil; Thorondor bears his body away, and Fingon takes the kingdom.
Fingolfin rides alone to the gate of Angband and challenges Morgoth to single combat.
Morgoth comes forth; Fingolfin wounds him seven times, but is beaten down and crushed.
Sauron is sent against Dorthonion, and its northward forest becomes Taur-nu-Fuin.
Haleth, aided by Beleg the Bowman out of Doriath, destroys an Orc-legion in Brethil.
Húrin and Huor are borne by Thorondor's eagles into the hidden city of Gondolin.
Húrin and Huor swear oaths of secrecy and are borne back to Dor-lómin.
Húrin asks leave of Turgon to depart, for the time of mortal men is short.
Maeglin begrudges the favour shown to Húrin and Huor, for he loved not the kindred of Men.

Then Turgon yielded to their prayer, and said: ‘By the way that ye came ye have leave to depart, if Thorondor is willing. I grieve at this parting, yet in a little while, as the Eldar account it, we may meet again.’
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Turgon welcomes Húrin and Huor, and they dwell in Gondolin wellnigh a year.
Beren slays the Orc-captain at Rivil's Well and regains his father's hand and the Ring of Felagund.
Gorlim betrays the lair at Tarn Aeluin; Barahir and his outlaws are slain, save Beren only.

Thereafter escaping from the Orcs Beren dwelt still in those lands as a solitary outlaw for four years, and did such deeds of single-handed daring that Morgoth put a price on his head no less than upon the head of Fingon King of the Noldor.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Círdan's ships land a force in Drengist, and Fingon has the victory upon the plains of Hithlum.
Galion is slain at Eithel Sirion, and Húrin his son drives the Orcs into the Anfauglith.
Morgoth renews his assaults, but Himring stands firm and his eastern army is broken by Thingol.
Maidros makes alliance with the Swarthy Men and gives them dwellings in and about Lothlann.
The Swarthy Men come out of Eriador north about Eryd Luin into Lothlann.
Beren forsakes Dorthonion and passes through the Girdle of Melian.

events.label: Beren, hard pressed, forsakes Dorthonion and passes the Girdle into Doriath
Húrin weds Morwen Elfsheen.
Húrin weds Morwen Elfsheen.

events.label: In this year at the mid-summer Beren son of Barahir met Lúthien Thingol’s daughter in the forest of Neldoreth, and because of her great beauty and his love a spell of dumbness was laid on him, and he wandered long in the woods of Doriath.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Túrin son of Húrin is born in Dor-lómin
Beren comes to Nargothrond, and Felagund knows his oath is come upon him
But Beren looked in the eyes of Melian, who spake not, and he took upon himself the Quest of the Silmaril, and went forth from Menegroth alone.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: But Lúthien with the aid of Húan, the hound of Valinor, who followed Celegorn but was won to the love of Lúthien, escaped from Nargothrond and came to Tol-in-Gaurhoth.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Celegorn and Curufin hinder the quest, and Nargothrond withholds its aid from the king.
Celegorn and Curufin speak against Felagund, and Nargothrond will not follow him
Dairon bewrays them, and Thingol demands a Silmaril as the bride-price of Lúthien
Felagund and Beren are unmasked by Sauron and cast into his pits
Felagund foretells that no son of Fëanor shall ever regain the Silmarils
Húan forsakes Celegorn to serve Lúthien, and Curufin's arrow smites Beren
Húan overthrows Sauron on Tol-sirion, and Sauron flees in shadow to Taur-nu-Fuin
In Sauron's pits the twelve are devoured; Felagund slays the wolf and is slain

In this year at the first spring Beren was released from his spell, and spoke to Lúthien, calling her Tinúviel, the Nightingale. Thus began the love of Beren the most renowned and Lúthien the most fair of which the Lay of Leithian was made.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Inglor casts off his crown, and ten faithful knights go forth with him
Lúthien escapes Thingol's tree-prison and is taken captive to Nargothrond
Lúthien frees Sauron's prisoners; Orodreth drives out Celegorn and Curufin
The Quest of the Silmaril (Beren & Lúthien)
events.cite: GA 465–466 (HoME XI) [C] — the Quest resolves across both annals, which is why the span is a span.

events.label: Thingol names a Silmaril as the bride-price of Lúthien; Beren takes the quest and seeks Felagund's aid.

Thus perished Inglor Felagund son of Finrod, fairest and most beloved of the children of Finwe, and returned never again to Middle-earth. But it is said that released soon from Mandos, he went to Valinor and there dwells with Amárië.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Beren cuts a Silmaril from the Iron Crown, and Curufin's knife snaps
Beren, before Thingol's throne, names himself Camlost
Beren, healed, leaves Lúthien sleeping and rides north alone to Taur-nu-Fuin
Carcharoth bites off Beren's hand; Thorondor bears them to the borders of Doriath
Húan wins Beren from death, and in the spring they come again to Menegroth
In the hames of Draugluin and Thuringwethil, Beren and Lúthien cross Anfauglith
Lúthien casts Carcharoth into slumber, and lays sleep upon Morgoth and all his hall
The Wolf-hunt of Carcharoth; Húan and the Wolf slay each other, and Beren dies
Thingol's mood is softened, and Beren and Lúthien are betrothed
Lúthien lays down her body at the first breaking of spring, and goes unto Mandos
Maidros begins the counsels called the Union of Maidros
Beren and Lúthien return to the world and dwell in Gwerth-i-guinar
Maidros makes his first trial of strength, and the Orcs are driven out of Beleriand
Birth of Dior Aranel the Beautiful, Thingol's heir, in Gwerth-i-Guinar
In this year Huor wedded Rían daughter of Belegund.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: And even so it came to pass; but it is not said that Húrin asked ever of Morgoth either mercy or death, for himself or for any of his kin.
events.cite: HoMe XI, The Grey Annals

events.label: Angband is emptied: wolves, a thousand Balrogs and Glaurung sunder the two hosts
At midsummer is fought the Fifth Battle, Nírnaeth Arnediad, upon the Anfauglith
Fingon, King of the Noldor, falls, overborne by the Balrogs
From that day begins the estrangement of Elves from Men, save the Three Houses
Gelmir of Nargothrond is hewn to death within sight of the Elves
Gwindor is taken, and Fingon is beaten back from the walls of Angband
Gwindor's wrath breaks the array, and Fingon leaps from the hills
Huor falls with the men of Hador, and Húrin is taken alive to Angband
Huor foretells that from his house and Turgon's a new star shall arise
Húrin and Huor hold the pass of Sirion, and Húrin bids Turgon go while time is
Húrin and Huor march away in the army of Fingon at the mustering of the hosts
Húrin, brought before Morgoth, defies him and is set in torment
Maeglin hears the words of Huor and marks them well, but says naught
Morgoth curses Húrin's kin and sets him in a chair of stone on Thangorodrim

date_basis_note.what_a_date_basis_means: THE INTEGER ON THIS AXIS IS THIS ARCHIVE'S OWN PLACEMENT, NOT A YEAR THE CORPUS RECORDS. The record's own bt/dt text says so in its own words; the integer beside it did not.
date_basis_note.published_for: ordering a person against others and drawing one numeric axis. A placement is not evidence of a date, and it must not be subtracted from, compared with, or otherwise arithmetic'd against a recorded year -- doing exactly that is what produced the contradictory parent-child pairs C494 (2) repairs. map/kinyear_check.py is the guard that now reads this field before it calls a pair contradictory.

the_four_kinds.AN ASSUMED LIFESPAN OFF A RECORDED YEAR: a span -- 85 years for Men, 500 for Elves, 250 for Dwarves -- subtracted from, or added to, the year on the record's other axis. Change the assumed span and the integer changes; nothing in the corpus does.
the_four_kinds.READ FROM THE RECORD'S OWN TEXT, WHICH Q: the record's own text names a year and hedges it -- 'before 455; not exact', 'c. F.o.A. 65 (estimated)'. The archive did not choose the number; it printed a hedged one as an exact one.
the_four_kinds.AN EDGE OF THE AXIS, NOT A YEAR AT ALL: the integer is an era boundary from this file's own `eras` block. 'Before Time' has no year and never will.
the_four_kinds.A PLACEMENT WITH NO STATED DERIVATION: neither the record's own text nor its other axis yields the number, and how it was arrived at is recorded nowhere. Saying so is the honest entry; a reconstructed derivation would be a second invention on top of the first.

date_basis_note.and_the_corpus_was_asked_first: map/corpus_birthyears.py took 69 birth years back out of HoME XII's own line-tables before this field was written -- years the archive had replaced with an assumed span while reading the DEATH year off the very same row. What carries a date_basis is what the corpus does not answer.
date_basis_note.and_the_per_row_entry_is_deliberately_te: site/arda_timeline.html embeds `chars`, so every byte on a record is published twice. What stands on the row is what DIFFERS per row -- the axis, the kind, the record's own words and the arithmetic. Everything that would read the same on all of them is here.

tradition_note.what: WHICH TEXT this row is read from, as an id registered in map/traditions.py -- not which volume, and not which tier. §X.11 asks for a chronology by age AND by textual tradition; by age was already built and its guard is chronology_check.
tradition_note.how: resolved from this row's own hand-written `cite` by map/traditions.py, which matches only sigla this archive writes -- AAm, GA, WJ Tale of Years, App A, App B, The Line of Elros, the line-tables, NoME, Silm -- and refuses ten strings by name with the reason and what would settle each.
tradition_note.not_derived_from: the volume, the corpus filename or the tier. C499 ruled the tier attaches to the content and not the file; C517 found 21 of 30 spans graded as Tolkien's own words were somebody else's book title printed inside a t1 volume, and t1_13_index.txt is wholly Christopher Tolkien's index. A tradition synthesised from a filename would repeat that one level up.
tradition_note.publication_layer_axis: one of C489's nineteen §IV values, INHERITED FROM THE TEXT rather than from the volume -- which is finer than C488's inheritance and never contradicts it, because first_publication dates a BOOK and this classifies a TEXT.
tradition_note.null_means_one_of_three: either the citation named no registered text; or it named a text that takes two of the nineteen at once (the 1977 Silmarillion is Tolkien's posthumous writing AND Christopher Tolkien's editorial arrangement, and §IV has no word for both); or `publication_layer_blocked_by` names an unidentified text cited beside the identified ones. It never means nobody looked.
tradition_note.blocked_by: the citation also names a text nobody identified, so the layer of the identified part cannot stand for the row. 122 character rows cite the appendices, Unfinished Tales and the Annals together without saying which annals; both appendices are lifetime publications and the annals may not be. WHAT WOULD SETTLE IT: a reader opening the note on each row and naming the annal.
tradition_note.where_the_prose_lives: map/traditions.py holds the register, the basis for every entry and every refusal. It is not repeated per record, on C494 (1)'s own discipline recorded in map/budget_check.py -- the cost was cut before the ceiling moved, and the standing explanation moved into one top-level note instead of onto every record.

type_basis_note: `type` is a LIST of the eight classes ruled in C932. A row's `type_basis` names how its list was arrived at; `C932-label` means it was derived from the event's own label by map/chronotype_axis.py, which is a saved instrument and can be re-run. The 220 rows carrying an empty list are not guessed at: they are listed in reports/CHRONOLOGY_TYPE_C932_2026-09-08.md to be READ against their loci, and each will carry its own basis when it is. `type_legacy`, where present, is the OLD single-value string and is NOT a translation of the new axis -- the two vocabularies never agreed.
